title: Scenario B: Post-Storm Nausea & Acute Radiation Dose Evaluation
trigger: Nausea, vomiting, headache, or acute fatigue following a Solar Particle Event (SPE)

doseVerification.arsThresholdDescription: CDC clinical guidance: Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) prodromal nausea/vomiting requires a whole-body absorbed dose >= 700-1000 mGy (0.7-1.0 Gy). Doses below 200 mGy make acute ARS clinically improbable.

otherCausesToRuleOut.indicator: Onset during initial 72 hours of microgravity; exacerbated by rapid head movements.
Check ECLSS ambient PCO2 > 3.0 mmHg; accompanied by frontal headache and lethargy.
Absence of elevated dosimeter reading; localized abdominal cramping or fever.

firstResponse.text: Verify storm status: if solar particle event is ongoing, ensure crew is inside the storm shelter (water wall / logistics shielding).
Immediately read and record personal electronic dosimeters (EPD) for all crew members.
Ensure sick bags and emesis bags with sealable ziplocks are readily accessible to prevent floating particulate hazards.

triage.question: Did active personal dosimeters record an absorbed dose >= 700 mGy during the storm?
Has repeated vomiting occurred within 2 hours of peak storm exposure?
Is the dosimeter reading under 200 mGy with symptoms limited to mild vestibular nausea?

rules.why: Early vomiting onset within 2 hours of significant dose is a documented marker of high-tier radiation prodrome.
Absorbed dose is well below the CDC threshold for acute radiation syndrome; evaluate vestibular or environmental causes.

steps.title: Radiation Dose Assessment
steps.text: Record EPD absorbed dose (mGy) and compare with habitat core dosimeters.

steps.title: Electrolyte Fluid Replacement
steps.text: Sip 250-500 mL of oral electrolyte rehydration solution slowly over 30 minutes to counteract fluid and mineral shifts.

steps.title: Antiemetic Administration
steps.text: Administer Ondansetron 4 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT) placed on the tongue. Allow to dissolve without swallowing whole.

steps.title: Serial Temperature & Infection Vigilance
steps.text: Monitor body temperature every 2 hours to screen for early immune compromise or concurrent infection.

doNot.text: Do NOT assume nausea is radiation sickness without verifying personal dosimeters and ruling out space motion sickness.
Do NOT leave emesis bags unsealed or unsecured in microgravity.
Do NOT administer antibiotics proactively during the prodromal phase without confirmed fever or clinical infection.

worseningSigns: Vomiting occurring within 60 minutes of exposure (high-dose indicator)
Inability to tolerate oral liquids, leading to dehydration
Hypotension (systolic BP < 90 mmHg) or extreme lethargy
holdPlan: Maintain hydration through small, frequent sips of electrolyte solution
Continue personal dosimetry logging every 60 minutes
Log time of all emesis episodes for biological dosimetry handoff to Earth
